slides.1.title: Cheese Pairings: Port's Perfect Partner
slides.1.html:
Cheese is Port's most important food pairing, with different styles of Port matching different styles of cheese.

🧀 Blue Cheese × Tawny (the golden rule of sweet with salty)

  • Stilton × 20 Year Tawny: the most traditional British Christmas pairing. The salty intensity of blue cheese needs the toffee sweetness of Tawny to balance it
  • Roquefort × 30 Year Tawny: the pungency of French blue cheese resonates perfectly with notes of coffee and chocolate
  • Gorgonzola × LBV: Italian blue is milder, and the fruity sweetness of LBV is enough to match it

🧀 Hard Aged Cheese × Ruby Reserve

  • Aged Manchego, Parmigiano Reggiano: the richness is cut through by Ruby's high acidity and black fruit
  • Portuguese Serra da Estrela (soft sheep's milk cheese) × 10 Year Tawny: a traditional Portuguese combination

🧀 Cheeses to Avoid

  • Fresh soft cheeses (Mozzarella/Ricotta): too delicate, overwhelmed by the Port
  • Washed-rind cheeses (Époisses): the fermented aroma is too strong and competes with the Port
slides.2.title: The Complete Guide to Port × Food Pairing
slides.2.items.0.label: Blue cheese × Tawny
slides.2.items.0.desc: Stilton/Roquefort × 20–30 Year Tawny: sweet with salty, the nutty toffee notes balancing the salty, savoury mould character. Widely regarded as one of the best pairings in the world
slides.2.items.1.label: Dark chocolate (70%+) × Vintage
slides.2.items.1.desc: High-cocoa dark chocolate × Vintage Port: bitter and sweet offset each other, with dried fruit and vanilla resonating with rich blackberry. The wine must be at least as sweet as the chocolate
slides.2.items.2.label: Portuguese custard tart (Pastel de nata) × LBV
slides.2.items.2.desc: The sweet creaminess of the custard tart × the black-fruit sweetness of LBV: Portuguese in spirit, with a perfect sweetness match
slides.2.items.3.label: Nut desserts × 30–40 Year Tawny
slides.2.items.3.desc: Walnut pie, almond brittle × 30–40 Year Tawny: the wine already has rich nutty notes, which echo the nut desserts rather than clash with them
slides.3.question: What is the most important principle when pairing Port with desserts?
slides.3.options.0: The wine must be less sweet than the food, for contrast
slides.3.options.1: Only unsweetened desserts can be paired
slides.3.options.2: The wine must be at least as sweet as the food, otherwise it tastes bitter and unbalanced
slides.3.options.3: Only Vintage Port can be paired with desserts
slides.3.explanation: "Wine at least as sweet as the food" is the golden rule of sweet wine pairing. If the food is sweeter than the wine, the wine's residual sugar seems insufficient and instead highlights its bitterness and acidity, creating an unpleasant imbalance. A very sweet chocolate cake therefore needs a sweeter Vintage or 30 Year Tawny to match it.
slides.4.question: What is Britain's most famous traditional Christmas Port pairing?
slides.4.explanation: Stilton blue cheese × 20 Year Tawny is Britain's most traditional Christmas pairing. The sweet and salty complement each other: Stilton's strong, salty, savoury blue character needs the toffee sweetness of Tawny to balance it, together creating an incomparable harmony.
